projects.title: Clinivara — Privacy-First Clinical Document Intelligence
projects.problem: Clinical laboratory reports contain high-risk PII/PHI (patient names, phone numbers, government IDs) that cannot legally or ethically be passed to public LLM APIs without de-identification.
projects.solution: An architectural 'Ironclad Privacy Shield' pipeline that runs OCR, identifies sensitive personal tokens using Microsoft Presidio and spaCy NER, cryptographically replaces them with entity tokens before LLM processing, validates extracted biomarkers against Pydantic schema gates, and outputs clinical explanations in English, Hindi, and Marathi.
projects.architecture: Clinical PDF/Scan Ingestion -> PyMuPDF & Tesseract OCR -> Presidio/spaCy PII Redaction Gate -> Clinical NER & Biomarker Parsing -> Pydantic Schema Validation -> Multilingual Guidance -> Audit Logging
verified_evidence: Pre-LLM privacy de-identification gate prevents data leakage
Pydantic clinical entity validation rejects out-of-range clinical anomalies
Multilingual explanations supported in English, Hindi, and Marathi
FastAPI asynchronous REST service architecture

projects.title: Agentic Clinical RAG — Multi-Agent Evidence-Grounded Retrieval
projects.problem: Monolithic LLM prompts hallucinate clinical citations and fail to detect critical patient contraindications buried deep inside unstructured medical text.
projects.solution: A stateful multi-agent architecture built with LangGraph decomposing retrieval into bounded, specialized agents: Researcher (hybrid fusion search), Skeptic (contraindication and provenance auditing), Scribe (structured citation synthesis), and Historian (audit state persistence).
projects.architecture: User Encounter Query -> Researcher Agent (Dense SentenceTransformers + Sparse BM25 Fusion) -> ChromaDB Vector Store -> Skeptic Safety Gate -> Scribe Structured Synthesis -> Historian Audit Trail
verified_evidence: 61/61 automated passing unit and integration tests
Hybrid linear weighted fusion combining semantic dense vectors and BM25 exact keyword matching
Strict ChromaDB startup validation verifying embedding space integrity
Evaluated on clinical benchmarks: 100% citation existence precision, 93.75% abstention specificity
Non-root multi-stage containerized deployment

projects.title: Production-Grade Airflow Weather ETL Pipeline
projects.problem: External REST APIs exhibit intermittent timeouts, schema drift, and network retries, causing partial database writes and duplicate records in downstream analytics.
projects.solution: An automated, containerized ETL pipeline orchestrated by Apache Airflow 3.x that queries the Open-Meteo REST API, performs schema cleaning with Pandas, and executes idempotent UPSERT operations into PostgreSQL backed by Docker Compose.
projects.architecture: Open-Meteo REST API -> Airflow TaskFlow HTTP Extract -> Pandas Transformation & Validation -> PostgreSQL Idempotent UPSERT -> Astronomer Runtime Monitoring
verified_evidence: Containerized orchestration with Astronomer runtime and Docker Compose
Idempotent database loading using SQL ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (UPSERT) pattern
Automated task retries with exponential backoff on network failures
Verified clean execution DAGs with healthy execution states

projects.title: Diabetes Inpatient 30-Day Readmission Risk System
projects.problem: Predicting 30-day diabetic readmission under severe class imbalance without data leakage between repeat hospital visits for the same patient.
projects.solution: A reproducible, leakage-free machine learning investigation on the UCI Diabetes 130-US Hospitals dataset (101,763 encounters across 71,515 patients). Enforced strict patient-grouped train/test splitting, ICD-9 clinical categorization, and cost-sensitive evaluation trade-offs.
projects.architecture: UCI EHR Data -> Patient-Grouped Stratified Split -> ICD-9 Clinical Grouping -> Missingness Indicator Encoding -> Logistic & Tree Classifiers -> Cost-Sensitive Threshold Tuning
verified_evidence: 101,763 hospital encounters and 71,515 unique patients analyzed
31 passing automated tests verifying pipeline reproducibility
Verified benchmark: ROC-AUC 0.6435, Recall 52.26%, Precision 16.48% under severe class imbalance
Explicitly documented clinical disclaimers regarding observational retrospective data

faq.question: What is Clinivara and how does it protect patient privacy?
faq.answer: Clinivara is a clinical document intelligence backend that processes medical lab reports and consultation notes. Its core engineering principle is zero-knowledge medical understanding: before any text reaches an LLM, a strict local PII de-identification gate (using Microsoft Presidio and spaCy NER) detects and sanitizes names, phone numbers, and IDs. Extracted clinical metrics are then verified against Pydantic schema validation rules, and explanations are generated in English, Hindi, and Marathi.

faq.question: How does your Clinical RAG system work?
faq.answer: Agentic Clinical RAG is a stateful multi-agent system built on LangGraph. Instead of a naive single-prompt RAG, it separates responsibilities across 4 bounded agents: Researcher (hybrid fusion search combining SentenceTransformers and BM25), Skeptic (evaluates evidence for contraindications and citation existence), Scribe (formats evidence-grounded recommendations), and Historian (preserves encounter audit trails). It has 61 automated tests verifying state transitions and ChromaDB vector index integrity.

faq.question: What was your hardest engineering challenge?
faq.answer: In the SWYNEX clinical readmission project, the primary challenge was preventing data leakage under extreme class imbalance. Because individual patients have multiple hospital visits across the 10-year dataset, random record-level train/test splits leaked patient-specific clinical trajectories into the validation set, creating artificially inflated metrics. The solution was implementing strict patient-level grouped splitting, ensuring no patient's encounters appeared in both train and test sets, yielding an honest, reproducible ROC-AUC of 0.6435.

faq.question: How do you evaluate retrieval quality in your RAG systems?
faq.answer: I evaluate RAG using multi-dimensional offline test harnesses: In-Scope Hit Rate@K, Citation Existence Precision (verifying that every generated clinical claim maps to an actual retrieved document ID), and Abstention Specificity (verifying that the system abstains or flags uncertainty when evidence is insufficient or contradictory rather than hallucinating).

faq.question: What technologies do you use for backend engineering and pipelines?
faq.answer: For backend engineering, I use Python, FastAPI, and Flask with Pydantic for strict runtime validation. For data engineering and orchestration, I use Apache Airflow 3.x with Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, and Pandas, implementing idempotent UPSERT patterns to ensure pipeline reruns never duplicate data.
